user.title: BLE Mesh Lights
user.description: Choose the ESPHome boards with the ble-adv-tx package that send to and listen for your lights.

data_description.boards: ESPHome boards running the ble-adv-tx package.
data_description.base_address: Lights get the addresses after this one (0x7E01, 0x7E02, …). Keep the default unless it clashes with other Bluetooth Mesh devices. It cannot be changed once a light is added.
data_description.command_interval: Shortest time between two commands to the same light.
data_description.outage_sensor: Optional. A binary sensor that turns on when mains power comes back after an outage and turns off again afterwards (a sensor that stays on is not suitable). Lights set to "Restore previous state" return to their last state then. Known limits: see "Known issues" in the integration's documentation.
data_description.power_cycle_gap: A light keeps advertising for about 7 s after it is switched off at the wall; in the first 30 minutes after it gets power it sends several messages a second. A silence of this many seconds after that counts as a possible short switch-off, and the light's state is marked uncertain. Shorter: catches quicker cycles, but a weak signal gives more false alarms. Cycles under about 7 s cannot be seen at all.

error.invalid_base_address: Enter a hexadecimal address from 0x0001 to 0x7F00.

confirm.title: Message counters lost
confirm.description: The file with the message counters is missing or damaged, while lights are paired. Starting again from zero would make every light ignore Home Assistant. Submit to continue with counters far above any earlier value.

address_collision.title: BLE Mesh Lights: address {address} used by another sender
address_collision.description: A message from {address}, one of the addresses Home Assistant sends as, did not come from Home Assistant. A remote or another system uses the same address, and the lights may ignore one of them. Factory-reset the affected light and add it again, or change the other sender's address.

init.title: New remote ({profile})
init.description: A remote with address {address} was heard for the first time. Bind it to the lights it controls, or ignore it (for example, a neighbour's remote).

bind.title: Bind to lamps
bind.description: Home Assistant follows this remote's presses on the chosen lamps.

profile_errors.title: BLE Mesh Lights: device profiles not loaded
profile_errors.description:
These device profiles could not be loaded, and lamps that use them stay unavailable:

{errors}

board_outdated.title: {board}: firmware package outdated
board_outdated.description: The board {board} reports ble-adv-tx package version {version}; BLE Mesh Lights needs version {required} or later. It still sends with the old version, but from version 2 the board sends a heartbeat event every 10 s, so an unplugged board is noticed within about 35 s instead of up to a minute (commands sent to it meanwhile are lost). Update the board's ESPHome firmware (see the board guide).

board_not_ready.title: {board} is not ready
board_not_ready.description: The board {board} is not connected, its action {action} does not exist, or (package 2) its heartbeat event esphome.ble_adv_tx.heartbeat does not arrive. Check that the board is online and runs the ble-adv-tx package.

board_sensor_disabled.title: {board}: BLE TX package sensor disabled
board_sensor_disabled.description: The diagnostic sensor "BLE TX package" of the board {board} is disabled. BLE Mesh Lights reads the board's firmware version from it, so it cannot send through this board. Enable the sensor in the board's device page, then reload BLE Mesh Lights (its menu → Reload).

user.title: Add a lamp
user.description: Choose the kind of light and how it should be called.

data_description.aliases: Other names for Assist, for example "street light".

power_cycle_timeout.title: No light found
power_cycle_timeout.description: No light was switched on within 2 minutes. Select Next to try again: switch the light off at the wall, wait about 15 seconds, and switch it on.

blinked.title: Did the light blink?
blinked.description: Home Assistant has just paired with {name}.

test_result.title: Did the light switch off and on?

test_failed_valen.title: The light did not react
test_failed_valen.description: Try the test again, start over from switching the light off and on, or reset the light: Switch the light off and on at the wall five times quickly.

remote.title: Remote
remote.description: {name} is ready. Bind its remote, so that Home Assistant follows the remote's presses?

remote_pair_valen.title: Remote
remote_pair_valen.description:
If the remote is already paired with this light, just select Next.

If not, pair it:
1. Switch the light off and on at the wall.
2. Right away, press and hold ON on the remote until the light blinks.
3. Release ON and press any button on the remote, for example OFF, to end pairing. While the remote's LED is on, the light ignores every command.

Then select Next.

remote_not_heard.title: No press heard
remote_not_heard.description: Home Assistant heard no button of a remote within a minute. A single press is sometimes lost on the air.

remote_heard.title: Remote {address}
remote_heard.description: Heard remote {address}, button "{button}". It controls now: {lamps}.

settings.title: Lamp settings
settings.description: Before you delete a lamp, reset it and pair its remote again: the integration never sends "unpair all".

settings_valen.title: Lamp settings
settings_valen.description: Before you delete a lamp, reset it (Switch the light off and on at the wall five times quickly.) and pair its remote again: the integration never sends "unpair all".

pair_again_valen.title: Pair again
pair_again_valen.description:
Pairs the light with Home Assistant again, for example after a factory reset. Its address, entities and automations stay.

Reset: switch the light off and on at the wall five times quickly.

Select Next, then switch the light off and on as the next screen says. A reset light blinks; one that was not reset does not, because it still knows Home Assistant. Then Home Assistant switches it off and on to check.

progress.power_cycle: Switch the light off at the wall, wait about 15 seconds, then switch it on. Home Assistant pairs with it as soon as it appears.
progress.test: Home Assistant switches the light off and on again.
progress.remote_press: Press any scene button on the remote.
progress.again_test: Home Assistant switches the light off and on again.

abort.not_loaded: BLE Mesh Lights is not running. Check the integration and try again.
abort.no_address_left: No address is left above the base address.
abort.remote_bound: Remote {address} is bound to {name}. Press a scene on the remote: the light's card shows it.
abort.reset_needed_valen: Reset the light, then add it again: Switch the light off and on at the wall five times quickly.
abort.reset_needed_again_valen: Reset the light, then pair it again: Switch the light off and on at the wall five times quickly. Then open the light's Reconfigure → Pair again.
abort.profile_failed: The light's profile failed to load; see the repair.

press_queue_full.message: Too many presses are waiting for this light; try again in a moment.

set_assumed_state.name: Set assumed state
set_assumed_state.description: Tells Home Assistant what the light looks like now, without sending anything (for example after it was changed by hand).

color_temp_kelvin.name: Color temperature
color_temp_kelvin.description: Color temperature in kelvin; the nearest one the light has is used.

brightness.name: Brightness
brightness.description: Brightness from 0 to 255; the nearest step the light has is used.

send_command.name: Send command
send_command.description: Sends one named command of the light's profile.

command.name: Command
command.description: A command id of the profile, for example relax or brightness_up.

queue.name: Queue
queue.description: Wait for the commands sent to the light before this one, as a remote press does. With queue a failed send does not raise: the answer's sent and reason tell (an unknown command still raises).

skip_sequence.name: Skip sequence forward
skip_sequence.description: Moves the light's message counter forward, for example after restoring an old backup, so the light does not ignore Home Assistant.

amount.name: Amount
amount.description: How far to move the counter forward.
